variants.title: Trace an image through BLIP-3
variants.context: BLIP-3 places visual and text tokens in one sequence. A frozen SigLIP encoder sees a downsized global view plus 384 pixel detail patches, a Perceiver resampler compresses each view into a fixed set of query tokens, assembly preserves the input's image and text order, and the language model predicts the next text token.
variants.prompt: One high resolution photograph and a short question arrive together. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Encode a downsized global view plus the 384 pixel detail patches the grid produces.
Predict the answer tokens autoregressively with self attention over both modalities.
Compress each encoded view into its fixed set of query tokens.
Accept the interleaved prompt containing the image and the question text.
Concatenate the sampled vision tokens with the tokenized question in source order.

variants.hint: Compression happens per view, before anything is concatenated.
variants.explanation: Every view is sampled independently and only then assembled, which is what keeps a high resolution image affordable in one sequence.

variants.title: Trace an image through BLIP-3
variants.context: BLIP-3 places visual and text tokens in one sequence. A frozen SigLIP encoder sees a downsized global view plus 384 pixel detail patches, a Perceiver resampler compresses each view into a fixed set of query tokens, assembly preserves the input's image and text order, and the language model predicts the next text token.
variants.prompt: A prompt alternates image, text, image, text as a two shot multimodal demonstration. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Resample every view of both images into its own group of query tokens.
Read the prompt as an interleaved sequence rather than as two separate image requests.
Generate the answer using self attention across all the assembled tokens.
Assemble the four segments so each image's tokens sit where that image appeared.
Encode a global view and detail patches for each of the two images.

variants.hint: What must survive assembly for a two shot demonstration to mean anything?
variants.explanation: Interleaved order is the evidence in a demonstration, so assembly places each image's tokens exactly where the image occurred.

variants.title: Trace an image through BLIP-3
variants.context: BLIP-3 places visual and text tokens in one sequence. A frozen SigLIP encoder sees a downsized global view plus 384 pixel detail patches, a Perceiver resampler compresses each view into a fixed set of query tokens, assembly preserves the input's image and text order, and the language model predicts the next text token.
variants.prompt: A receipt photograph has its total printed in very small type and the detail patch cap is set low. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Resample those views into query tokens and discard the finer patch features.
Assemble the surviving vision tokens beside the question text.
Encode only the global view and the few detail patches the cap allows.
Admit the receipt image with a question that asks for the printed total.
Return an answer that cannot state the total, because no admitted view ever carried it.

variants.hint: Can a later stage recover evidence an earlier stage dropped?
variants.explanation: Visual evidence must stay identifiable after compression; once the sampler discards a small label, the language model cannot reason it back.

variants.title: Follow the training curriculum
variants.context: The BLIP-3 curriculum builds capabilities in stages: base resolution alignment, then high resolution and text rich data with any resolution sampling, then single image instruction tuning, then multi image instruction tuning. Each stage changes the evidence distribution the model has seen.
variants.prompt: A team reproduces the reported BLIP-3 recipe end to end. Put the stages in order.

items.text: Mix multi image examples with a subset of single image data to restore interleaved behavior.
Align vision and language at 384 by 384 resolution on caption, OCR, grounding, and interleaved mixtures.
Fine tune on the single image instruction mixture for one epoch, including pure text instructions.
Add high resolution and text rich data with any resolution sampling and the long side patch grids.

variants.hint: Resolution comes before instructions, and single image comes before multi image.
variants.explanation: Each stage changes the evidence distribution, so skipping one removes a capability that a later stage assumes is present.

variants.title: Follow the training curriculum
variants.context: The BLIP-3 curriculum builds capabilities in stages: base resolution alignment, then high resolution and text rich data with any resolution sampling, then single image instruction tuning, then multi image instruction tuning. Each stage changes the evidence distribution the model has seen.
variants.prompt: After multi image tuning, single image accuracy has dropped noticeably. Put the events in order, ending with the fix.

items.text: High resolution pretraining added text rich and detailed visual evidence.
Re run the multi image stage with a subset of single image data mixed in.
Single image instruction tuning taught the model to follow task instructions.
Multi image tuning on multi image data alone eroded the single image behavior.
Base resolution alignment produced general image language ability.

variants.hint: The last stage decides which earlier abilities survive.
variants.explanation: Mixing single image data into the multi image stage is what keeps multi image gains from unnecessarily erasing single image ability.

variants.title: Follow the training curriculum
variants.context: The BLIP-3 curriculum builds capabilities in stages: base resolution alignment, then high resolution and text rich data with any resolution sampling, then single image instruction tuning, then multi image instruction tuning. Each stage changes the evidence distribution the model has seen.
variants.prompt: A product needs strong reading of small text in documents. Put the curriculum choices in order.

items.text: Add the higher resolution OCR mixture when any resolution sampling is introduced.
Include base resolution OCR data in the first alignment stage.
Verify multi page behavior in the multi image stage before claiming document support.
Keep document instructions in the single image instruction mixture.

variants.hint: Text reading is built by data at each stage, not by one late fine tune.
variants.explanation: Capability is curated by evidence type across stages, so a late narrow fine tune cannot supply what the earlier mixtures never contained.

variants.title: Budget the visual tokens
variants.context: A BLIP-3 planning estimate rounds the 384 pixel patch grid up on each side, caps detail patches at 12, adds one downsized global view per image, and charges 128 query tokens for every view. The modeled input total is prompt tokens plus visual tokens plus the reserved answer tokens.
variants.prompt: One image is 1200 by 900 pixels and the detail patch cap is 12. How many visual tokens does the planning model charge?
variants.hint: Count the views first, and do not forget the one that is not a detail patch.
variants.explanation: The grid rounds up to 4 by 3, so 12 detail patches plus one global view is 13 views, and 13 times 128 is 1664 tokens.

mistakes.feedback: Left the downsized global view out of the view count.
Rounded the patch grid down to 3 by 2 instead of up.

variants.title: Budget the visual tokens
variants.context: A BLIP-3 planning estimate rounds the 384 pixel patch grid up on each side, caps detail patches at 12, adds one downsized global view per image, and charges 128 query tokens for every view. The modeled input total is prompt tokens plus visual tokens plus the reserved answer tokens.
variants.prompt: Two images are each 800 by 800 pixels and the request sets a detail patch cap of 3. How many visual tokens does the planning model charge in total?
variants.hint: The cap is applied per image, after the grid is computed.
variants.explanation: The grid asks for 9 patches but the cap allows 3, so each image contributes 4 views, and 2 times 4 times 128 is 1024 tokens.

mistakes.feedback: Used the 9 patch grid and ignored the cap of 3.
Charged one image instead of both.

variants.title: Budget the visual tokens
variants.context: A BLIP-3 planning estimate rounds the 384 pixel patch grid up on each side, caps detail patches at 12, adds one downsized global view per image, and charges 128 query tokens for every view. The modeled input total is prompt tokens plus visual tokens plus the reserved answer tokens.
variants.prompt: One image is 1500 by 400 pixels with a detail patch cap of 12, the prompt is 512 tokens, and 512 tokens are reserved for the answer. What is the modeled input total?
variants.hint: The total has three parts, and only one of them depends on the image.
variants.explanation: The grid rounds up to 4 by 2, so 8 detail patches plus the global view is 9 views and 1152 visual tokens; adding the prompt and the reserve gives 2176.

mistakes.feedback: Left out the reserved answer tokens.
Dropped the global view from the view count.

variants.title: Operate the checkpoint deliberately
variants.context: An open multimodal checkpoint is an operational commitment. Pin the revision, preprocessing, tokenizer, and prompt template together, check the current license for the intended use, set image and patch limits before allocating accelerator memory, and fail closed on unreadable evidence in high impact workflows.
variants.prompt: A commercial product wants to ship the referenced xGen-MM instruction checkpoint. What has to happen first?
options: Confirm that the checkpoint loads with the installed transformers version.
Verify the current model and dataset licenses for the intended commercial use.
Reproduce the paper's benchmark scores on the same public evaluation sets.
optionFeedback: Loading successfully is necessary for engineering, but it is not the blocking question here.
Correct: the model card lists a non commercial license for that checkpoint and directs commercial users to Salesforce.
Benchmark parity says nothing about whether the product is allowed to ship the weights.
variants.hint: Which check can stop the project regardless of how well the model performs?
variants.explanation: License and dataset terms are release blocking and can change, so they are verified for the specific checkpoint and use before any engineering commitment.

variants.title: Operate the checkpoint deliberately
variants.context: An open multimodal checkpoint is an operational commitment. Pin the revision, preprocessing, tokenizer, and prompt template together, check the current license for the intended use, set image and patch limits before allocating accelerator memory, and fail closed on unreadable evidence in high impact workflows.
variants.prompt: Tail latency is spiking, but the dashboard only shows requests per second and average latency. What should the team add?
options: Latency and memory broken down by patch count per request.
A higher alerting threshold so the spikes stop paging the team.
More replicas until the average latency returns to its old value.
optionFeedback: Correct: a request with 13 views costs far more than one with 2, so patch count is the dimension that explains the tail.
Raising the threshold hides the signal without changing what the system does.
Adding capacity pays for the imbalance instead of revealing which requests cause it.
variants.hint: What varies between two requests that both count as one request?
variants.explanation: Visual tokens scale with views per image and image count, so latency and memory are tracked by patch count rather than by request count alone.

variants.title: Operate the checkpoint deliberately
variants.context: An open multimodal checkpoint is an operational commitment. Pin the revision, preprocessing, tokenizer, and prompt template together, check the current license for the intended use, set image and patch limits before allocating accelerator memory, and fail closed on unreadable evidence in high impact workflows.
variants.prompt: A claims workflow receives a scan too blurred for any patch to resolve the policy number. What should the system do?
options: Fail closed and route the case to a human instead of answering.
Return the model's best guess with a low confidence label attached.
Retry with the maximum patch grid until an answer appears.
optionFeedback: Correct: high impact workflows fail closed when the evidence is unreadable.
A confidence label does not make an invented policy number safe to act on.
More patches cannot add detail that the pixels never contained.
variants.hint: Does more compute create evidence that is not in the image?
variants.explanation: Unreadable evidence is a terminal state in high impact workflows, because sampling harder cannot recover detail the image does not hold.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Each part of BLIP-3 has one job: the global view keeps scene context, detail patches keep local evidence, the query tokens bound sequence length, ordered assembly keeps interleaved inputs answerable, and the curated datasets each build a named capability.
variants.prompt: Match each element of any resolution encoding to what it contributes.

pairs.label: Downsized global view
pairs.detail: Keeps whole scene context that no single detail patch can see.

pairs.label: 384 pixel detail patch
pairs.detail: Preserves small text, chart marks, and local spatial detail at native scale.

pairs.label: Query tokens per view
pairs.detail: Bounds how much sequence length each encoded view is allowed to consume.

pairs.label: Ordered sequence assembly
pairs.detail: Keeps images and text in their source positions so interleaved prompts stay answerable.

variants.hint: One of these controls cost rather than evidence.
variants.explanation: Any resolution encoding trades evidence against sequence length, so each part either supplies evidence or bounds what that evidence costs.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Each part of BLIP-3 has one job: the global view keeps scene context, detail patches keep local evidence, the query tokens bound sequence length, ordered assembly keeps interleaved inputs answerable, and the curated datasets each build a named capability.
variants.prompt: Match each reported symptom to the design decision that most likely caused it.

pairs.label: A serial number in the corner never appears in any answer
pairs.detail: The detail patch cap was set below what the image needed.

pairs.label: The model answers about the second image when asked about the first
pairs.detail: Image and text order was not preserved during assembly.

pairs.label: A single request overruns the language model input budget
pairs.detail: Views per image times query tokens was never checked against the budget.

pairs.label: Answers describe fragments and miss the overall setting
pairs.detail: The downsized global view was dropped from the encoded views.

variants.hint: Three of these are budget decisions and one is an ordering decision.
variants.explanation: Compression and assembly choices are the ones that decide which evidence is still identifiable when the language model reads the sequence.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Each part of BLIP-3 has one job: the global view keeps scene context, detail patches keep local evidence, the query tokens bound sequence length, ordered assembly keeps interleaved inputs answerable, and the curated datasets each build a named capability.
variants.prompt: Match each curated dataset family to the capability it is meant to build.

pairs.label: BLIP3-OCR-200M
pairs.detail: Reading text in images at base resolution.

pairs.label: BLIP3-OCR-HD-30M
pairs.detail: Reading text in higher resolution and text dense images.

pairs.label: BLIP3-GROUNDING-50M
pairs.detail: Relating described objects to their locations in the image.

pairs.label: Interleaved web documents
pairs.detail: Learning from image and text demonstrations in their natural order.

variants.hint: Curate by capability, not by file format.
variants.explanation: The framework treats the data recipe as part of the system, so each capability the product needs has to be present in the mixture.
